questions.prompt: What ecological role can crocodilians fulfill in wetlands?
options: Decomposers that digest dead leaves
Pollinators that fertilize aquatic plants
Herbivores that maintain grasslands through grazing
Predators that influence prey populations and the ecosystem

questions.prompt: What group do caimans belong to?
options: To the gavialids, with the gharials
To the family Alligatoridae, alongside alligators
With squamates, with monitor lizards
To Crocodylidae, with real crocodiles

questions.prompt: Why do gharials particularly depend on waterways?
options: Its powerful legs allow it to pursue terrestrial prey
Its body and muzzle are adapted to aquatic hunting for fish
Its nostrils are adapted to deep sea diving
Its short snout is used to crush aquatic plants.

options: Algae that they graze on the water’s edge
Small invertebrates and accessible animals
Prey as large as adults
Milk provided by their mother after hatching

options: Front legs transformed into fins
Lateral movements of the neck that pull the body
A muscular tail that provides much of the propulsion
Webbed feet that produce all the thrust alone

questions.prompt: How do crocodilians hear underwater?

They only hear sounds transmitted through the air
Protected hearing structures can transmit sound vibrations
Their nostrils pick up sound waves instead of ears

questions.prompt: Which living group does the sphenodon, also called tuatara, belong to?
options: In the Testudines, like the turtles
Rhynchocephali, distinct from lizards
To Squamates, like snakes and lizards
To Crocodilians, like gharials

An extra pair of moving eyes behind the ears
An olfactory organ exposed at the top of the skull
A transparent third eyelid that closes both eyes

A humid tropical climate where temperatures are constantly high
An arid desert where temperatures often exceed those of tropical reptiles
A polar climate where adults remain active under the ice

Embryonic development only resumes after several years
The eggs are incubated by the female inside her body
Eggs hatch a few days after laying

Two rows of upper teeth that overlap a lower row
A single row of upper teeth that fit between two lower rows
A horny beak with no teeth on the jaws

questions.prompt: Which birds does the tuatara sometimes share its burrow with on some islands?

Albatrosses that build nests in burrows
Penguins breeding on islands
Kiwis that live in trees

questions.didYouKnow: The tuatara sometimes shares its island burrows with petrels.

questions.prompt: How do chameleons often catch insects?
options: With a quickly projected tongue and finished with an adhesive surface
With sticky fingers that catch insects from a distance
By projecting a viscous saliva onto the prey
With jaws with long teeth that grab insects
questions.explanation: The chameleon's tongue can be projected quickly; its adhesive end grabs prey before being brought back into the mouth.

options: They can orient each eye independently
They are fixed and the entire head rotates to scan the landscape
They are placed frontally for permanent binocular vision
They always look in the same direction and never converge

options: Claws that retract under the skin
Adhesive pads similar to those of geckos
Fingers grouped into opposing pincers
Long fingers united in a broad webbing
questions.explanation: The fingers are grouped in opposing bundles which form a strong grip around the branches.

The tail carries the eggs during laying
The tail helps balance the chameleon while it runs on the ground
The tail helps the chameleon grip branches

questions.prompt: Where is the greatest diversity of chameleons found?
options: In Madagascar
In Central Asia
In the Caribbean Islands
In Southern Africa only

questions.didYouKnow: The chameleon's tongue can be projected quickly to grasp prey.

questions.prompt: What sound do some geckos make?

Vocalizations only possible underwater
Sounds produced only by the rubbing of their paws
Sound calls used to echolocate prey

They widen the visual field in the midday sun
They collect more light in the darkness

questions.prompt: What is the common name crested gecko?

A desert gecko with a ruff around its neck
An arboreal gecko with reliefs above the eyes and along the back

Of mammals that they kill by constriction
Nectar sucked from the bottom of the flowers

The division of an individual into two adult animals

Regulate temperature by dissipating heat

To evacuate waste and participate in reproduction
